explication:
<explanation>
1. Identify the project type and purpose
   - From the file tree and README, Mythic is a Swift/SwiftUI macOS application—an open-source game launcher and GUI frontend for the Legendary CLI.  
   - It coordinates multiple subsystems (Engine for DirectX support, Wine, Legendary CLI, Epic Games auth, Discord RPC, auto-updates via Sparkle) to manage, download, and launch Windows games on macOS.

2. High-level architecture layers
   - Presentation Layer  
     • All SwiftUI views under `Mythic/Views` (Navigation, Unified modules, Sheets, Windows)  
     • `MythicApp.swift`, `ContentView.swift` → entry point and root view  
   - ViewModel / Presentation Logic  
     • ViewModel classes in `Mythic/Views/Unified/Models` (e.g., `GameCardVM`, `GameListEvoVM`)  
     • Bind the UI to business services  
   - Domain/Business Logic Layer  
     • `Mythic/Utilities`  
       – Engine interfaces (`Engine.swift`, `EngineExt.swift`) for DirectX  
       – `LegendaryInterface.swift` & `LegendaryInterfaceExt.swift` call the embedded Legendary Python CLI  
       – `WineInterface.swift` & `WineInterfaceExt.swift` invoke Wine to run Windows binaries  
       – `LocalGames.swift` / `LocalGamesExt.swift` manage scanning local game containers  
       – `VariableManager.swift`, `FileLocations.swift` manage env vars and file paths  
       – `SparkleController.swift` for auto-update checks  
       – `NetworkMonitor.swift` for offline/online state  
   - Data Access / Utilities  
     • JSON parsing via SwiftyJSON  
     • ZIP handling via ZIPFoundation  
     • SemanticVersion for version parsing  
     • Caching images via swiftui-cached-asyncimage  
   - Persistence  
     • UserDefaults (via extension) for settings  
     • On-disk container metadata and downloaded game files  
   - External / Third-party Dependencies  
     • Legendary CLI (embedded Python environment in `Mythic/legendary/_internal`)  
     • Wine (dynamic libs under `Mythic/Utilities/Wine`)  
     • Metal-based UI libs: ColorfulX, Glur  
     • Sparkle (auto-updates)  
     • Discord RPC (via SwordRPC extension)  
     • Epic Games WebAuth (via SwiftUI WebView)  

3. Relationships and interactions
   - UI Layer → ViewModels → calls Business Logic services  
   - Business Logic → invokes external engines/CLIs (Engine, Legendary, Wine)  
   - Business Logic → reads/writes container metadata & game downloads on the file system  
   - Business Logic → persists settings to UserDefaults  
   - SparkleController periodically checks for updates → notifies UI  
   - NetworkMonitor broadcasts connectivity changes to Presentation Layer  
   - Epic WebAuth window issues authentication → returns tokens to LegendaryInterface  

4. Architectural patterns & design principles
   - MVVM: Views bind to ViewModels, which orchestrate domain services  
   - Layered architecture: clear separation of Presentation, Domain Logic, Data/Infrastructure, External Services  
   - Dependency inversion: protocols/extensions allow mocking Legendary/Wine interfaces for testing  
   - Single responsibility: each Utility class focuses on one subsystem (Engine, Wine, Legendary, Networking)  

5. Tailoring the system design diagram
   a. Draw 4 horizontal layers (top to bottom):  
      1) Presentation (SwiftUI)  
      2) ViewModel / Orchestration  
      3) Domain Logic / Services  
      4) Data & External Services  
   b. In each layer, group components:  
      - Presentation: `NavigationView`, `Unified Modules`, `Sheets`, `Windows`  
      - ViewModel: `GameCardVM`, `GameListEvoVM`, etc.  
      - Domain Logic: EngineService, LegendaryService, WineService, LocalGamesService, SparkleController, NetworkMonitor  
      - Data: FileLocations, UserDefaults, JSON Parser, ZIP Handler, SemanticVersion  
      - External: Legendary Python CLI, Wine dylibs, Epic WebAuth endpoint, Discord RPC, Sparkle Updater  
   c. Draw arrows to show calls:  
      - UI → VM → Domain Services → External  
      - Domain Services → Data Access → File System / UserDefaults  
      - SparkleController → Sparkle framework → GitHub Releases  
      - LegendaryService → embedded Python CLI → Legendary servers  
   d. Annotate technologies on each box (e.g., “Sparkle (Auto-Update)”, “SwiftyJSON”, “ZIPFoundation”, “Metal – ColorfulX/Glur”).

6. Diagram styling guidelines
   - Use consistent shapes/colors by layer:  
     • Blue rectangles for Presentation  
     • Green for Domain Services  
     • Orange for External dependencies  
     • Gray for Data/Persistence  
   - Label every component clearly (e.g., “LegendaryInterface”)  
   - Use solid arrows for synchronous calls; dashed for async or event notifications (NetworkMonitor updates).  
   - Include a legend explaining color/shapes.  

7. Additional tips
   - Zoom out: show macOS application boundary containing your layers.  
   - Emphasize that Mythic bundles an internal Python framework and dynamic libraries for cross-platform game execution.  
   - Highlight extension points (protocols for Engine/Wine/Legendary) so new backends (e.g., Steam) can plug in.  
   - Capture that all persistent state lives locally—no central backend.  

By following this layered breakdown, you’ll have a system design diagram that is both faithful to Mythic’s code structure and clearly communicates how each component collaborates to deliver the game-launching experience on macOS.  
</explanation>
